[PAPER_0085, relevance_score=0.345] To begin to address these issues, we conducted an exploratory mixed ANOVA wherein experiment (1, 2) served as the between-participants factor, current trial modality (visual, auditory) and modality transition (repeat, switch) served as the within-participants factors, and the CSE in mean probe RT served as the dependent measure. We made two predictions. First, if S-R mappings serve as boundaries for the CSE, then overall CSE magnitude should be lower in Experiment 2 than in Experiment 1.

[PAPER_0088, relevance_score=0.269] Finally, experiment and modality transition did not interact, F < 1. Consistent with the binary coding view, this outcome suggests that task sets and S-R mappings serve as independent boundaries for the CSE. Because this finding comes only from an exploratory analysis, however, future studies will be needed to test this hypothesis in an a priori fashion.

[PREREG_0004, relevance_score=0.375] q4: There are 2 hypotheses.

1. The CSE will remain modality-specific as in our prior studies for either or both of two reasons. First, participants can easily categorize each trial as "visual" or "auditory" (Hazeltine et al., 2011). Second, participants will respond only to the probe in each trial, which reduces CSE magnitude, rather than to both the prime and probe, which increases CSE magnitude (Grant & Weissman, 2019).

[PREREG_0005, relevance_score=0.356] Critically, this hypothesis predicts a 3-way interaction among modality condition (repeat, switch), previous trial congruency (congruent, incongruent), and current trial congruency (congruent, incongruent).

2. The CSE will not remain modality-specific for one of two reasons. First, participants may have time to silently read the distractor word on the screen before the target word appears.

[PREREG_0007, relevance_score=0.431] This hypothesis assumes that one must switch to the current-trial task set before one can "apply" one's memory of previous-trial congruency to modulate the response cued by the distractor in the current trial. These hypotheses predict an interaction between previous trial congruency and current trial congruency (i.e., a CSE) but not necessarily a 3-way interaction among modality condition, previous trial congruency, and current trial congruency.

[PAPER_0076, relevance_score=0.285] [From Experiment 1, cited for: Data analysis] Following the exclusions above, we conducted separate, repeated-measures ANOVAs on mean probe RT and mean probe ER.

[From Experiment 1, cited for: Data analysis] There were four within-participants factors in each ANOVA: current trial modality (visual, auditory), modality transition (repeat, switch), trial N - 1 congruency (congruent, incongruent), and trial N congruency (congruent, incongruent).

[PAPER_0085, relevance_score=0.283] To begin to address these issues, we conducted an exploratory mixed ANOVA wherein experiment (1, 2) served as the between-participants factor, current trial modality (visual, auditory) and modality transition (repeat, switch) served as the within-participants factors, and the CSE in mean probe RT served as the dependent measure. We made two predictions. First, if S-R mappings serve as boundaries for the CSE, then overall CSE magnitude should be lower in Experiment 2 than in Experiment 1.
items.paper_content_summary: Experiment 2 analyzed mean probe RT and error rate by condition. An exploratory mixed ANOVA also used CSE magnitude in mean probe RT as its dependent measure. [PAPER_0076] [PAPER_0085]

[PREREG_0007, relevance_score=0.309] This hypothesis assumes that one must switch to the current-trial task set before one can "apply" one's memory of previous-trial congruency to modulate the response cued by the distractor in the current trial. These hypotheses predict an interaction between previous trial congruency and current trial congruency (i.e., a CSE) but not necessarily a 3-way interaction among modality condition, previous trial congruency, and current trial congruency.

items.registration_content_summary: The registration specified mean RT and mean error rate in each condition, analyzed with congruency factors in repeated-measures ANOVAs. It described the CSE as an interaction between previous and current trial congruency. [PREREG_0013] [PREREG_0015] [PREREG_0007]
items.deviation_information:
The paper uses CSE magnitude in mean RT as a derived dependent measure in an exploratory mixed ANOVA, rather than only analyzing condition means with congruency factors. This transformation for analysis was not found in the provided registration excerpts. Its exploratory framing is disclosed but does not remove the deviation. [PAPER_0085] [PREREG_0015] [PREREG_0007]

[PAPER_0057, relevance_score=0.377] We excluded participants who did not complete the task (one), did not follow the task instructions (one), experienced technical (i.e., computer-related) difficulties (one), and/or performed the task with less than 75% accuracy (three). We conducted our analyses on data from the remaining 32 participants (16 male, 16 female; 31 right-handed, one left-handed; 17-26 years old, M = 18.66, SD = 1.49).

[PAPER_0074, relevance_score=0.382] Data Analysis

The data analysis was identical to that in Experiment 1 (see Appendix C for supplemental ANOVAs that include this factor). On average, 5.9% of the trials were errors and .8% were outliers.

[From Experiment 1, cited for: Data analysis] Before analyzing the data, we excluded several trial types.

[PAPER_0075, relevance_score=0.386] [From Experiment 1, cited for: Data analysis] Prior to analyzing mean probe response time (RT), we excluded practice trials, the first trial of each block, outliers (i.e., trials with RTs > 3 SD from the conditional mean), omitted responses, incorrect responses (i.e., errors), and trials immediately following omitted responses and errors.

[From Experiment 1, cited for: Data analysis] Prior to analyzing mean probe error rate (ER), we excluded the same trial types with the exception of errors, which were the dependent measure.
items.paper_content_summary: For RT analysis, omitted responses and trials immediately following omissions were excluded. For error-rate analysis, the paper says the same trial types were excluded except errors, implying omissions were excluded. One participant who did not complete the task was also excluded. [PAPER_0075] [PAPER_0057]

[PREREG_0016, relevance_score=0.401] q22: We will exclude participants whose overall accuracy during the twelve blocks of test trials is lower than 75%. If this occurs, then our final sample size will be larger than 32 participants. However, we will only include data from the first 32 participants with usable data (i.e., overall accuracy greater than 75%) in the final analyses.

With regard to these 32 participants, we will exclude the following trials from analysis.

[PREREG_0017, relevance_score=0.418] With regard to these 32 participants, we will exclude the following trials from analysis. In the analysis of mean RT, we will exclude errors, trials following errors, response omissions, trials following response omissions, and outliers (i.e., trials with RTs more than 3 standard deviations from their conditional means). In the analysis of mean ER, we will exclude the same trials with the exception of errors and response omissions, which are the dependent measure.

q23: We will replace each participant who performs the task with less than 75% overall accuracy.
items.registration_content_summary: Omitted responses and trials following them were to be excluded from RT analysis. For error-rate analysis, omissions were to be retained as part of the dependent measure, while trials following omissions were excluded. The registration specified retaining the first 32 participants with usable data. [PREREG_0017] [PREREG_0016]
items.deviation_information:
The paper’s stated error-rate exclusions imply that omitted responses were excluded, whereas the registration specified retaining them in the dependent measure. [PAPER_0075] [PREREG_0017] The paper also excluded a participant for noncompletion; an exclusion rule for incomplete participation was not found in the provided registration excerpts. [PAPER_0057] [PREREG_0016]
